# Integrity standards, dependencies, and fixture sources

## Public standards

- [RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.html): JCS; section 3.2.2
  serialization, section 3.2.3 UTF-16 property ordering, Appendix B binary64
  vectors. `jcs-vectors.json` transcribes the 26 Appendix B rows; null expectations
  identify the nonfinite rows that must be refused. These test the canonicalizer
  component, independently of Basisline's narrower numeric input profile.
- [RFC 7493 sections 2.1–2.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7493.html): I-JSON
  UTF-8, Unicode, numbers, and duplicate-member requirements. Basisline's exact
  integer/canonical-closure restrictions are additional profile requirements.
- [RFC 8259](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html): JSON grammar.
- [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339.html): date/time syntax; the
  existing year-zero/leap-second implementation limitations remain unresolved.
- [CommonMark 0.31.2](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/): literal escaping,
  blockquotes, character references, and hard line breaks.
- [FIPS 180-4](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4): SHA-256. Known-answer
  tests include empty input, `abc`, and one million ASCII `a` characters.

The Markdown golden files are independently specified expected template bytes;
they are not generated by invoking the renderer inside a test. The receipt
contains ordinary fractional evidence, full timestamp precision, and optional
revision/conflict data. The outcome includes multiline and structural-injection
strings. Tests preserve and compare their final LF.

## Pinned release artifacts

`package-lock.json` records exact registry URLs and SHA-512 integrity values.
Selected direct release tarballs were inspected before installation, including
implementation entry points, package metadata, and licenses. Installation uses
`--ignore-scripts`; no development branches or runtime browser dependencies are
introduced. Pinning provides reproducibility, not proof of trustworthy code.

| Package | Version | License | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| canonicalize | 5.1.0 | Apache-2.0 | RFC 8785 adapter, no runtime dependencies |
| jsonc-parser | 3.3.1 | MIT | Scanner and strict throwing visitor, no runtime dependencies |
| commonmark | 0.31.2 | BSD-2-Clause | Independent test parser only |
| entities | 3.0.1 | BSD-2-Clause | Locked commonmark test dependency |
| mdurl | 1.0.1 | MIT | Locked commonmark test dependency |
| minimist | 1.2.8 | MIT | Locked commonmark test dependency |

Release artifacts:
[canonicalize](https://registry.npmjs.org/canonicalize/-/canonicalize-5.1.0.tgz),
[jsonc-parser](https://registry.npmjs.org/jsonc-parser/-/jsonc-parser-3.3.1.tgz),
[commonmark](https://registry.npmjs.org/commonmark/-/commonmark-0.31.2.tgz).

Review boundaries: canonicalize handles UTF-16 sorting and ECMAScript primitive
serialization and rejects nonfinite numbers/lone surrogates. Its arbitrary-object
features (`toJSON`, boxed values, omission of undefined) are not exposed through
the byte API. jsonc-parser is permissive by default: Basisline separately rejects
comments/scanner errors, validates raw tokens before numeric conversion, throws
on visitor errors, disables trailing commas/empty input, and detects decoded
duplicates before assignment. Tests exercise these wrappers, not only libraries.
commonmark is test-only; it is not loaded by generation or verification.

Future dependency changes require re-review of release artifacts and rerunning
the standards/adversarial corpus. No claim is made of an external security audit
or exhaustive vulnerability-database coverage.
